version: 1.1

source: eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_gsd

comment: "HEDIS GSD (Glycemic Status Assessment) for the diabetes population aged\
  \ 18-75, computed live over the gold evidence base. Denominator = eligible diabetes\
  \ patients. Compliant (Blood Sugar Controlled) = last A1c of the measurement year\
  \ is 9.0% or below. HEDIS indicators over the eligible population: Good Control\
  \ Rate (last A1c < 8.0%) and Poor Control Rate (last A1c > 9.0% OR no A1c test).\
  \ HEDIS-aligned demo, not NCQA-certified."

dimensions:
  - name: Measurement Year
    expr: measurement_year
    comment: HEDIS measurement year the metrics are computed for (e.g. 2026).
    display_name: Measurement Year
    synonyms:
      - year
      - reporting year
      - MY

  - name: Compliance Status
    expr: CASE WHEN evidence_value <= 9.0 THEN 'MET' ELSE 'NOT_MET' END
    comment: "Computed live: MET = last A1c of the measurement year is 9.0% or below\
      \ (Blood Sugar Controlled); NOT_MET = last A1c above 9.0% or no A1c test. The\
      \ rule lives in this metric view, not in gold."
    display_name: Compliance Status
    synonyms:
      - status
      - met status
      - adherence status
      - gap status

  - name: Clinic
    expr: clinic_id
    comment: Clinic (site) the patient's panel belongs to. Enables care-gap and compliance
      rates by site.
    display_name: Clinic
    synonyms:
      - clinic
      - site
      - location
      - facility

  - name: Panel
    expr: panel_id
    comment: PCP panel the patient belongs to.
    display_name: Panel
    synonyms:
      - panel
      - pcp panel
      - provider panel
      - care team

  - name: Gap Reason
    expr: CASE WHEN evidence_value <= 9.0 THEN 'Met' WHEN evidence_datetime IS NULL
      THEN 'No A1c test in measurement year' ELSE 'Last A1c above 9%' END
    comment: "Computed live: why the patient is a care gap (NOT_MET); 'Met' when compliant.\
      \ Group care gaps by reason."
    display_name: Gap Reason
    synonyms:
      - gap reason
      - reason
      - care gap reason
      - why gap

  - name: Age Band
    expr: CASE WHEN age < 45 THEN '18-44' WHEN age < 65 THEN '45-64' ELSE '65-75'
      END
    comment: Age band at the end of the measurement year (eligible population is 18-75).
    display_name: Age Band
    synonyms:
      - age group
      - age bracket
      - age range

  - name: Measure
    expr: measure_id
    comment: HEDIS measure code; this view reports GSD (Glycemic Status Assessment).
    display_name: HEDIS Measure
    synonyms:
      - measure id
      - hedis measure
      - quality measure

measures:
  - name: Eligible Patients
    expr: COUNT(1)
    comment: Diabetes patients aged 18-75 eligible for GSD (the measure denominator).
      One row per patient.
    display_name: Eligible Patients
    format:
      type: number
      decimal_places:
        type: exact
        places: 0
    synonyms:
      - denominator
      - eligible population
      - eligible count
      - patients eligible

  - name: Tested Patients
    expr: COUNT(1) FILTER (WHERE evidence_datetime IS NOT NULL)
    comment: Eligible patients with at least one A1c test in the measurement year
      (not a HEDIS indicator; testing coverage).
    display_name: Tested Patients
    format:
      type: number
      decimal_places:
        type: exact
        places: 0
    synonyms:
      - tested patients
      - a1c tested
      - patients with an a1c

  - name: Compliant Patients
    expr: COUNT(1) FILTER (WHERE evidence_value <= 9.0)
    comment: Eligible patients whose last A1c of the measurement year is 9.0% or below
      (Blood Sugar Controlled; the measure numerator) — computed live from the evidence.
    display_name: Compliant Patients
    format:
      type: number
      decimal_places:
        type: exact
        places: 0
    synonyms:
      - numerator
      - compliant count
      - patients met
      - blood sugar controlled
      - controlled patients

  - name: GSD Compliance Rate
    expr: MEASURE(`Compliant Patients`) / MEASURE(`Eligible Patients`)
    comment: Share of eligible diabetes patients whose last A1c of the measurement
      year is 9.0% or below (Blood Sugar Controlled; the inverse of the HEDIS GSD
      > 9.0% indicator). Re-aggregates at any grain.
    display_name: GSD Compliance Rate
    format:
      type: percentage
      decimal_places:
        type: max
        places: 1
    synonyms:
      - compliance rate
      - gsd rate
      - blood sugar controlled rate
      - met rate

  - name: Good Control Patients
    expr: COUNT(1) FILTER (WHERE evidence_value < 8.0)
    comment: Patients whose latest measurement-year A1c is < 8.0% (good glycemic control)
      — band computed live from evidence_value.
    display_name: Good Control (<8%) Patients
    format:
      type: number
      decimal_places:
        type: exact
        places: 0
    synonyms:
      - good control
      - well controlled
      - a1c under 8

  - name: Good Control Rate
    expr: MEASURE(`Good Control Patients`) / MEASURE(`Eligible Patients`)
    comment: "HEDIS GSD < 8.0% indicator: share of eligible patients whose last A1c\
      \ of the measurement year is below 8.0%."
    display_name: Good Control (<8%) Rate
    format:
      type: percentage
      decimal_places:
        type: max
        places: 1
    synonyms:
      - good control rate
      - a1c under 8 rate

  - name: Poor Control Patients
    expr: COUNT(1) FILTER (WHERE evidence_value > 9.0 OR evidence_datetime IS NULL)
    comment: "Patients whose last A1c of the measurement year is above 9.0%, or who\
      \ had no A1c test (HEDIS counts a missing test as > 9.0%)."
    display_name: Poor Control (>9%) Patients
    format:
      type

Measure Eligible ages Numerator (compliant when…) Threshold / definition GSD — Glycemic Status Assessment 18–75 Last HbA1c of the measurement year ≤ 9.0% (blood sugar controlled) Reported as two rates over all eligible patients: < 8.0% (good control) and > 9.0% (poor control; a missing test counts as > 9.0%). General target < 7.0% KED — Kidney Health Evaluation 18–85 BOTH an eGFR test AND a uACR test in the year Both components required; either alone is a gap BPD — Blood Pressure Control 18–75 Most recent BP reading controlled Controlled = systolic < 140 mmHg AND diastolic < 90 mmHg SPD — Statin Therapy 40–75 Dispensed a statin during the year Moderate-to-high intensity statin EED — Eye Exam 18–75 Retinal / diabetic eye exam in the year Dilated or retinal-imaging exam; biennial if prior exam normal and low risk A1c is identified by LOINC Component "Hemoglobin A1c" across methods (e.g. 4548-4 default, 17856-6 HPLC, 59261-8 IFCC). eGFR and uACR are the two required kidney components of KED.

A single population A1c threshold is **not** appropriate for every adult with diabetes. The target range is
individualized by comorbidity burden and life expectancy:
| Patient profile | Target A1c range |
|---|---|
| No or minimal microvascular complications, >10 years life expectancy | 6.0–7.0% |
| Moderate comorbidity, 5–10 years life expectancy | 7.0–8.0% |
| Marked comorbidity or end-stage disease, <5 years life expectancy | 8.0–9.0% |
This is the key difference from the GSD quality **measure**, which applies the same two cut-offs to everyone: the
last A1c of the year below 8.0% (good control) or above 9.0% (poor control, where a missing test also counts as
poor). The measure answers *"how controlled is the population?"*; the protocol answers *"what should this specific
patient's target be?"*.

- Check HbA1c **every 3 months** for patients who are above individualized goal or whose therapy has changed.
- Check HbA1c **every 6 months** for patients who are stable at goal.
- Do not react to a single out-of-range HbA1c; confirm with a repeat before escalating therapy.
The GSD measure reads only the **last** A1c of the measurement year, so it cannot distinguish a patient checked
quarterly from one checked once.

Effective **measurement year 2026**, the Glycemic Status Assessment (GSD) numerator accepts a **Glucose
Management Indicator (GMI)** derived from continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) as an equivalent glycemic-status
result, alongside a laboratory **HbA1c**. The GMI result is identified by **LOINC 97506-0**; HbA1c remains
**LOINC 4548-4** (and method variants). A patient with a qualifying GMI but no lab HbA1c is now **compliant**.
Operational impact: the GSD value set gains a code for MY2026. A patient who looked like a care gap under the
MY2025 value set (CGM data only, no lab draw) flips to compliant under MY2026 — a pure **measure-drift** event
driven by a value-set version change, not by any change in the patient's data.

> Synthetic payer memo for the Care Protocol Context & Ontology demo. HEDIS-aligned, not NCQA-certified, not
> for clinical use. This memo **supersedes** the MY2025 glycemic-status guidance for measurement year 2026.

GSD, Glycemic Status Assessment, covers diabetics aged 18–75 and uses the last A1c of the measurement year in eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_gsd. GSD compliance, also called Blood Sugar Controlled, GSD rate, or blood sugar controlled rate, is COUNT_IF(gold_adherence_gsd.evidence_value <= 9.0) / COUNT(*). Good Control Rate, also called good glycemic control or controlled diabetes, is COUNT_IF(gold_adherence_gsd.evidence_value < 8.0) / COUNT(*). Poor Control Rate, also called poor glycemic control or uncontrolled diabetes, is COUNT_IF(gold_adherence_gsd.evidence_value > 9.0 OR gold_adherence_gsd.evidence_datetime IS NULL) / COUNT(*). Each denominator is all eligible patient rows in the selected scope, not only tested patients; missing tests are not compliant. Compliance and good control answer different questions because the former includes A1c values from 8.0 through 9.0.

A single population A1c threshold is **not** appropriate for every adult with diabetes. The target range is
individualized by comorbidity burden and life expectancy:
| Patient profile | Target A1c range |
|---|---|
| No or minimal microvascular complications, >10 years life expectancy | 6.0–7.0% |
| Moderate comorbidity, 5–10 years life expectancy | 7.0–8.0% |
| Marked comorbidity or end-stage disease, <5 years life expectancy | 8.0–9.0% |
This is the key difference from the GSD quality **measure**, which applies the same two cut-offs to everyone: the
last A1c of the year below 8.0% (good control) or above 9.0% (poor control, where a missing test also counts as
poor). The measure answers *"how controlled is the population?"*; the protocol answers *"what should this specific
patient's target be?"*.

These are **measurement** changes. The underlying clinical care protocol (A1c targets, cardiorenal
pharmacotherapy, screening cadence) is unchanged. Updating a measure value set is not the same as updating the
standard of care — the demo deliberately distinguishes the two.

Over-treatment carries real harm. Consider **de-intensifying** glucose-lowering therapy and re-targeting a
higher A1c when a patient is over-controlled relative to their individualized goal — for example an older
adult with chronic kidney disease and a history of hypoglycemia whose A1c is 6.5%.
For adults **aged 65 and older**, prefer drug classes **other than insulin, sulfonylureas, and meglitinides**
to minimize hypoglycemia risk. Age-stratified hypoglycemia-avoidance is absent from the HEDIS measures.

Effective **measurement year 2026**, the Glycemic Status Assessment (GSD) numerator accepts a **Glucose
Management Indicator (GMI)** derived from continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) as an equivalent glycemic-status
result, alongside a laboratory **HbA1c**. The GMI result is identified by **LOINC 97506-0**; HbA1c remains

## eGFR in the Care Protocol: Measures, MY2026 Codes, and Where It's Defined

**KED (Kidney Health Evaluation) is the only quality measure that uses eGFR.** For MY2026, a single LOINC code counts: **`98979-8`** (CKD-EPI 2021). Two care-protocol medication rules also reference eGFR thresholds, but they are contraindication rules, not quality measures. [Prior eGFR analysis](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/a57cc2ab04a2425899ab01fe07da4667?o=7474653847172668)

### Where eGFR Is Used

| Context | How eGFR is used | Protocol source |
|---|---|---|
| **KED** (diabetes patients, ages 18–85) | One of two required numerator tests — a patient needs both an eGFR *and* a uACR test in the measurement year | `CP sec5`: `KED monitoredBy LP-EGFR` [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/7d933272400146bbac6d423d6cfc4148?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_521c83) [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-8e0e87c6-ec71-4cc4-bc5a-cfd3232063ea) |
| **SGLT2 inhibitors** | Contraindicated when eGFR < 20 | `CP sec4`: `DRUGCLASS-SGLT2 contraindicatedWhen eGFR_LT_20` [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/7d933272400146bbac6d423d6cfc4148?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_521c83) |
| **Biguanides (Metformin)** | Contraindicated when eGFR < 30 | `CP-GLY-2`: `DRUGCLASS-BIGUANIDE contraindicatedWhen eGFR_LT_30` [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/7d933272400146bbac6d423d6cfc4148?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_521c83) |

GSD, SPD, BPD, EED, and MAD do **not** use eGFR.

### LOINC Codes That Count as eGFR, by Measurement Year

<!-- begin-embedded:query_78f627 -->
| value_set_version | segment_name | egfr_loinc_codes | code_count |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2025 | Kidney eval - eGFR (KED) | 33914-3, 98979-8 | 2 |
| 2026 | Kidney eval - eGFR (KED) [MY2026 modernized: CKD-EPI only] | 98979-8 | 1 |
<!-- end-embedded:query_78f627 -->

- **MY2025**: two codes — `33914-3` (MDRD) and `98979-8` (CKD-EPI)
- **MY2026**: one code — `98979-8` (CKD-EPI only) — the segment name explicitly says *"MY2026 modernized: CKD-EPI only"* [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/7d933272400146bbac6d423d6cfc4148?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_78f627)

### Where It's Defined

1. **Code list** — the `KED_EGFR` segment in the value-set table [eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.value_set_segment](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/explore/data/eli_test_classic_catalog/care_protocol_terminology/value_set_segment?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668). Each row is tied to a `measurement_year`, so the MY2026 row carries only `98979-8`. You match lab results on `loinc_code = code` for the segment and year you want. [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-edda8620-a170-4029-82f4-21a22de79a49) [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-c5a7f603-0689-491a-9666-2c038996db63)
2. **Measure logic & thresholds** — the protocol-edges table [eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.protocol_edges](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/explore/data/eli_test_classic_catalog/care_protocol_terminology/protocol_edges?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668), which records the `monitoredBy` and `contraindicatedWhen` relationships shown above.
3. **Glossary page** — *eGFR (Estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate)* [eGFR (Estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate)](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/150dfd59-85b9-4efd-8014-bb170bfe626e?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668) — lists both LOINC codes and identifies eGFR as one of KED's two tests. Note: this page has **not** been updated for MY2026 and still lists `33914-3`.

### Caveat on the MY2026 Change

Dropping `33914-3` (MDRD) from the MY2026 value set could theoretically lower KED rates if the lab data still uses that code. However, in this synthetic dataset, all lab results from 2023 onward already use `98979-8` (CKD-EPI), so the change has no practical impact on MY2025 or MY2026 KED. It would only matter for historical lookbacks to 2022 or earlier. [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-ed62bbb6-6537-45d5-9de2-05957f4f1f00)

source: eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_gsd

comment: "HEDIS GSD (Glycemic Status Assessment) for the diabetes population aged\
  \ 18-75, computed live over the gold evidence base. Denominator = eligible diabetes\
  \ patients. Compliant (Blood Sugar Controlled) = last A1c of the measurement year\
  \ is 9.0% or below. HEDIS indicators over the eligible population: Good Control\
  \ Rate (last A1c < 8.0%) and Poor Control Rate (last A1c > 9.0% OR no A1c test).\

  - name: Measurement Year
    expr: measurement_year
    comment: HEDIS measurement year the metrics are computed for (e.g. 2026).
    display_name: Measurement Year
    synonyms:
      - year
      - reporting year
      - MY

  - name: Compliance Status
    expr: CASE WHEN evidence_value <= 9.0 THEN 'MET' ELSE 'NOT_MET' END
    comment: "Computed live: MET = last A1c of the measurement year is 9.0% or below\
      \ (Blood Sugar Controlled); NOT_MET = last A1c above 9.0% or no A1c test. The\

      - status
      - met status

    synonyms:

      - care team

      - gap reason
      - reason
      - care gap reason

    INNER JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.protocol_edges e
        ON e.subject = am.drug_class
        AND e.predicate = 'contraindicatedWhen'
    INNER JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.protocol_edges a
        ON a.subject = e.object
        AND a.predicate = 'appliesTo'
    INNER JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.loinc_parts lp

    COUNT(DISTINCT patient_id) AS patient_count,
    COUNT(DISTINCT patient_id) OVER () AS total_distinct_patients_across_all_drugs
FROM combined

A single population A1c threshold is **not** appropriate for every adult with diabetes. The target range is
individualized by comorbidity burden and life expectancy:
| Patient profile | Target A1c range |
|---|---|
| No or minimal microvascular complications, >10 years life expectancy | 6.0–7.0% |
| Moderate comorbidity, 5–10 years life expectancy | 7.0–8.0% |
| Marked comorbidity or end-stage disease, <5 years life expectancy | 8.0–9.0% |
This is the key difference from the GSD quality **measure**, which applies the same two cut-offs to everyone: the
last A1c of the year below 8.0% (good control) or above 9.0% (poor control, where a missing test also counts as
poor). The measure answers *"how controlled is the population?"*; the protocol answers *"what should this specific
patient's target be?"*.

CP-ESC-1 (statin gap). A patient aged 40–75 with diabetes and no statin dispensed in the year (SPD gap) should be started on a moderate-to-high intensity statin , after confirming no contraindication (pregnancy, active hepatic disease). CP-ESC-2 (kidney gap). A patient missing eGFR or uACR (KED gap) should have the missing component ordered. If uACR ≥ 30 mg/g, start an ACE inhibitor or ARB (not both). CP-ESC-3 (combined cardiorenal). A patient with diabetes and chronic kidney disease (N18.*) and heart failure (I50.*) is a cardiorenal priority: ensure statin, ACE/ARB, and an SGLT2 inhibitor (if eGFR ≥ 20), and monitor A1c every 3 months. Escalation rules reference measures (GSD/KED/SPD), labs (eGFR, uACR, A1c), diagnosis families (E10/E11/E13, N18, I50) and drug classes — the relationships this protocol contributes to the knowledge graph.

- Check HbA1c **every 3 months** for patients who are above individualized goal or whose therapy has changed.
- Check HbA1c **every 6 months** for patients who are stable at goal.
- Do not react to a single out-of-range HbA1c; confirm with a repeat before escalating therapy.
The GSD measure reads only the **last** A1c of the measurement year, so it cannot distinguish a patient checked
quarterly from one checked once.

Effective **measurement year 2026**, the Glycemic Status Assessment (GSD) numerator accepts a **Glucose
Management Indicator (GMI)** derived from continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) as an equivalent glycemic-status
result, alongside a laboratory **HbA1c**. The GMI result is identified by **LOINC 97506-0**; HbA1c remains
**LOINC 4548-4** (and method variants). A patient with a qualifying GMI but no lab HbA1c is now **compliant**.
Operational impact: the GSD value set gains a code for MY2026. A patient who looked like a care gap under the
MY2025 value set (CGM data only, no lab draw) flips to compliant under MY2026 — a pure **measure-drift** event
driven by a value-set version change, not by any change in the patient's data.

## 73 GSD-Eligible Diabetics Aged 65–75 Had A1c Above 9% and No Statin in MY2026

Of the GSD-eligible diabetics aged 65–75 in measurement year 2026, **73 patients** had a last A1c above 9% (through 2026-10-30) **and** no statin dispensed in MY2026 through 2026-10-30. ### Definitions Used

- **A1c above 9%**: the patient's last A1c of MY2026 is strictly above 9.0% — the GSD poor-control threshold. A result of exactly 9.0% does not count. Patients with no A1c test are excluded since they have no A1c above 9%. [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-788eac61-11a7-482a-9d5c-eac964e04174) [GSD — Glycemic Status Assessment for Patients With Diabetes](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/09e5fd5b-c4ed-42a7-bf34-a009c6771444?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668)
- **No statin**: the patient has no statin dispensed in MY2026 in the SPD statin-therapy measure data (through 2026-10-30). Statins are matched from drug ingredients to specific products ordered via RxNorm subsumption. Every GSD patient aged 65–75 also appears in the SPD data, since SPD covers ages 40–75. [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-7408a2b2-dea4-490f-ab3c-0f41d8901eca) [SPD — Statin Therapy for Patients With Diabetes](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/c8324591-625b-44db-9f8b-c57e9ba5dd7b?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668)
- **The 2026-10-30 cutoff**: the data naturally ends near that date — the latest A1c is from 2026-10-30 and the latest statin order is from 2026-10-28, with zero statin orders after the cutoff. [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/f9b5bb3b63ed467894e368fbdd3bce4e?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_b4fbc0)

The certified Genie space returned **72** rather than 73. The difference is one patient whose A1c was recorded on 2026-10-30 at 07:53 AM (A1c = 11.2%). The Genie's timestamp comparison (`<= '2026-10-30'`) treated the cutoff as midnight, excluding that intra-day record. The corrected SQL includes the full day, yielding **73**. [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/f9b5bb3b63ed467894e368fbdd3bce4e?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_526a6b)
